title: Image Analysis of Immediate Early Gene Expression in Spinal Cord Sections
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bakmicu6
materials: .Export the combined image as a TIFF.

steps.title: Open image and create mask layer
steps.instruction: Using Adobe Photoshop (or similar) open the spinal cord section image and create a new layer for the mask.

substeps.instruction: Open spinal cord section image in Photoshop
Create a new layer for the mask

steps.title: Paste mask and align with Free Transform
steps.instruction: Paste the mask onto the image (adds a new layer) and use the Free Transform tool to scale and rotate the mask until it aligns with the image.

substeps.instruction: Paste mask onto image (adds new layer)
Use Free Transform to scale and rotate mask to align

steps.title: Refine alignment using Warp tool
steps.instruction: Right‑click the mask layer, choose the Warp tool, and adjust the mask to further align it with the image.

substeps.instruction: Right‑click mask layer
Select Warp and adjust alignment

steps.title: Open TIFF in FIJI
steps.instruction: Open the TIFF file that contains the image with the overlaid mask in ImageJ (FIJI, NIH).

substeps.instruction: Open TIFF file with overlaid mask in FIJI

steps.title: Initialize Cell Counter plugin
steps.instruction: In FIJI, go to Plugins → Analyse → Cell Counter → Initialize → Add to set up counting.

substeps.instruction: Navigate Plugins → Analyse → Cell Counter → Initialize → Add

steps.title: Select region cell number
steps.instruction: Select the cell number that corresponds to the region being counted (e.g., Type 1 = Laminae 1); each number defines a separate region.

substeps.instruction: Select cell number corresponding to region (e.g., Type 1 = Laminae 1)

steps.title: Mark cells in region
steps.instruction: Click on each cell within the selected region to record its coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Click on each cell in the region

steps.title: Repeat counting for all regions
steps.instruction: Change the cell number as needed and repeat the clicking process for every region of interest.

substeps.instruction: Change cell number as needed
Repeat clicking for each region

steps.title: Export cell coordinates file
steps.instruction: Save the generated .txt file containing the X‑Y coordinates of each marked cell.

substeps.instruction: Save .txt file with X‑Y coordinates

steps.title: Open image and copy mask
steps.instruction: Open the neuron image and its corresponding mask, select the entire mask area, and copy it.

substeps.instruction: Open neuron image and its mask
Select whole mask area
Copy mask

steps.title: Draw vector paths with Magnetic Pen
steps.instruction: In Photoshop, open Window → Paths, select the Magnetic Pen tool, and draw vector paths following color and brightness transitions; press Enter to finish each path.

substeps.instruction: Open Window → Paths panel
Select Magnetic Pen tool
Draw vector paths following color/brightness transitions
Press Enter to end each path

steps.title: Set path tolerance level
steps.instruction: Adjust the tolerance level for the paths (lower values give tighter adherence, higher values produce smoother curves).

substeps.instruction: Adjust tolerance level (lower = tighter, higher = smoother)

steps.title: Save mask as transparent PNG
steps.instruction: Export the path‑based mask as a .png file, ensuring the transparency option is selected during export.

substeps.instruction: Export mask as .png with transparency enabled

steps.title: Import tilescans and reconstruct 3D
steps.instruction: Import completed tilescan images into TissueMaker (MicroBrightField Bioscience), order, rotate, and align them using structural landmarks, then visualize the reconstructed spinal cord in 3D with Neurolucida 360.

substeps.instruction: Import tilescan images into TissueMaker
Order, rotate, and align images using structural landmarks
Visualize reconstructed spinal cord in 3D with Neurolucida 360
